Previously `slug` was set only when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` (`...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`) and `requestedSlug` was set only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` (`...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`). The diff changes this to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`, meaning when team billing is disabled, neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug` is written, and when enabled, both are written. This matches the finding’s claim of broken slug creation/approval-flow behavior based on the shown logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch searches event.destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId, but externalCalendarId is falsy in that ternary branch, so the find never matches and selectedCalendar is always undefined. Rescheduling any booking whose stored reference lacks externalCalendarId (bookings created before that field was persisted) issues calendar.events.update with calendarId: undefined, which the Google client rejects with 'Missing required parameter: calendarId' (or a 404 against /calendars/undefined); the pre-diff code fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId and the update succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, `selectedCalendar` is now computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. In the ternary’s fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined by definition, so the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and will not match any normal calendar entry, yielding `undefined`. This regresses from the pre-diff fallback (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and can lead to calling `calendar.events.update` with `calendarId` undefined for bookings/references without `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent uses the same dead predicate — find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy — so calendarId is undefined whenever the reference's externalCalendarId is missing. Cancelling a booking without a stored externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId: undefined and the Google client rejects it, so the event stays on the host's calendar while the booking is cancelled in the database and the cancellation API reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the `deleteEvent` (and similarly `updateEvent`) fallback branch is logically dead: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, so it will almost always return `undefined`, leaving `calendarId` unset (or forcing an unintended fallback elsewhere). This matches the finding that deletions can fail or target the wrong calendar when the reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, causing the booking to be cancelled in DB while the external event remains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createAllCalendarEvents silently drops a destination when its credentialId resolves to nothing — neither in this.calendarCredentials nor returned by the prisma.credential.findUnique lookup (or the fetched credential has no app slug) — because the if (credential) block has no else branch, no log, and no failure EventResult. A collective booking against a host whose destinationCalendar references a deleted credential completes and is reported as success while that host's calendar event is never created, with no log and no failed EventResult to indicate the dropped work — the host confirms a meeting that never appears on their calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`, the branch `if (destination.credentialId)` attempts to resolve a credential from `this.calendarCredentials`, else falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` and only reconstructs `credential` if `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug`. If both lookups fail (deleted credential, missing from in-memory list, or DB record without `app.slug`), execution reaches `if (credential) { ... createEvent ... }` with no `else` branch: nothing is pushed to `createdEvents`, no log, and no failure `EventResult` is produced. That matches the finding that a destination can be silently dropped, leading to missing calendar event creation with no indication in the returned results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent selects the target calendar by matching cal.credentialId === credentialId and falls back to 'primary' on no match, so destinationCalendar rows with a null credentialId — precisely the case createAllCalendarEvents handles by filtering credentials by integration type and calling createEvent(c, event) without an externalId — get their events created on the user's primary calendar instead of the specified destination. Hosts whose destinationCalendar has a null credentialId get booking events silently created on their Google primary calendar instead of the selected destination calendar (previously destination.externalId was used), and the booking reference is persisted with externalCalendarId: undefined, so later reschedules/cancellations of those bookings cannot locate the event and fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)`, the target calendar is selected via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and if no match it uses `"primary"` (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination has **no** `credentialId`, it iterates credentials by `destination.integration` and calls `createEvent(c, event)` **without** passing `destination.externalId` (and `CalendarManager.createEvent` does not use its new `externalId?` param to influence calendar selection; it always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`). Therefore, for destinations with `credentialId == null`, Google events will be created on the user's primary calendar instead of the specified `destination.externalId`, and the resulting `EventResult.externalId` will be `undefined` in that branch, meaning later update/delete paths relying on `externalCalendarId` in references may not be able to target the intended calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent derives eventsUrl from the first destinationCalendar entry regardless of which host's credential the service instance was constructed with, so for a collective event every non-first Office365 host's event is created against the first host's calendar id using their own token. On a collective booking with multiple Office365 hosts, every host after the first has their event created via /me/calendars/<first host's externalId>/events authenticated with their own token, which Microsoft Graph rejects with 404 — their calendars silently end up with no event while the booking is reported as created.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and for COLLECTIVE team events `handleNewBooking` appends additional hosts' destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` now destructures only the first entry (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and derives `eventsUrl` from that calendar’s `externalId`. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, events are created for multiple credentials (either per `destination.credentialId` or by filtering `this.calendarCredentials`), but the same `event` object (with an array of destination calendars) is passed each time; nothing selects the destination calendar matching the current credential. This means non-first Office365 hosts will still attempt to create via `/me/calendars/<first externalId>/events` using their own token, which is inconsistent and can fail (e.g., 404), matching the reported behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent always uses the first destinationCalendar entry's externalId as the Lark calendarId rather than the entry matching the invoked credential, so non-first Lark hosts on a collective event target the first host's calendar with their own token. Collective bookings with more than one Lark host fail event creation for every host after the first (Lark rejects the foreign calendarId), so those hosts' calendars never receive the event while the booking proceeds as successful.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` (and related methods) now derive `calendarId` from the *first* element only: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`. Meanwhile, collective events can populate `evt.destinationCalendar` with multiple hosts’ destination calendars (`handleNewBooking.ts` pushes team members’ destinationCalendars for `COLLECTIVE`). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` then iterates destinations and invokes `createEvent` per credential, but passes the same `event` object containing the full destinationCalendar array for every host. There is no Lark-side selection by the invoked credential (unlike Google, which added `credentialId`-based selection). This means non-first Lark hosts will still try to create using the first host’s `externalId` (calendarId) with their own token, which is consistent with the reported failure mode (Lark rejecting foreign calendar IDs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The CalDAV create path filters the invoked credential's calendars against the first destinationCalendar entry's externalId, so when the service is invoked for a different host's destination on a collective event no calendar of that credential matches and the filter yields an empty list. For multi-host (collective) bookings, every CalDAV host whose destination is not first in the list gets zero event-creation calls (or an immediate failure from the empty response set), so their calendar never receives the event with no per-host error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (BaseCalendarService / CalDAV path), `createEvent` now destructures only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and then filters the credential’s `calendars` list to only those whose `externalId` matches that first entry (`calendars.filter((c) => mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : true)`). With the diff converting `destinationCalendar` to an array and for collective events pushing additional hosts’ destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` in `handleNewBooking.ts`), invoking CalDAV event creation for a non-first host/credential can result in the filter producing an empty set (because that credential’s calendars won’t match the first host’s `externalId`), causing zero CalDAV event creation calls for that host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] loadUsers' catch rewrites every non-HttpError, non-Prisma error into a 500 'Unable to load users' without logging the original error, including the deliberate plain-Error guard 'dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.' thrown two lines above. A malformed client request (empty/missing users list on a dynamic link) is reported as a 500 instead of a 4xx, the guard's message never reaches the caller, and because nothing is logged the operator debugging a failing booking has no trace of the root cause — any unexpected error inside loadUsers is fully swallowed.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` now wraps its logic in a `try/catch`. It deliberately throws a plain `Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` when `dynamicUserList` is missing/empty, but the `catch` only rethrows as a 400 when the error is an `HttpError` or `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError`. That plain `Error` falls into the generic branch and is rewritten to `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`, losing the original message and returning a 500 for what is effectively a malformed request. The diff also shows no logging of the original error in this `catch`, so the root cause is dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewritten catch in EventManager's update path drops the console.error(message) that previously recorded failures, and returns calendarReference?.map(...) ?? [], which is an empty array whenever the throw happens before calendarReference is assigned (e.g. the newBooking prisma lookup inside the same try). A database failure during a reschedule/update is now returned as an empty result list — indistinguishable from 'no calendar references to update' — with no log line at all, so the caller proceeds as if nothing needed updating, the calendar event is left stale, and the failure is invisible to both the user and operators.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the `catch` block in the update flow no longer logs `console.error(message)` and now returns `Promise.resolve(calendarReference?.map(...) ?? ([] as Array<EventResult<...>>))`. Since `calendarReference` is initialized as `undefined` (`let calendarReference: PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined`) and is only assigned later inside the `try` (after DB lookups like `prisma.booking.findUnique`), any exception thrown before `calendarReference` is set will cause the catch to return `[]`. That is indistinguishable from the legitimate early-return case `if (calendarReference.length === 0) return [];`, so failures can be silently swallowed with no log and no error result object.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When a calendar reference's credentialId resolves to neither a user credential nor a database credential, the if (calendarCredential) block falls through with no else branch, no log, and no error result, silently skipping that reference's deleteEvent. Cancelling such a booking reports success while the event remains on that host's calendar, and operators get no log indicating which reference was skipped; this is the common configuration since deleting a credential is itself the trigger for cancelling that credential's future bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, within the new loop over `bookingCalendarReference` (now an array), the branch `if (credentialId) { ... }` sets `calendarCredential` from `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and then tries `prisma.credential.findUnique` as a fallback. If both lookups fail, execution simply exits that `if (credentialId)` branch with no `else`/logging/result pushed to `apiDeletes`, so that reference’s `deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` is silently skipped. This matches the finding: missing handling when a reference’s `credentialId` cannot be resolved, leading to undeleted remote events with no operator signal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The recurring-cancellation branch iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials (the organizer's) and takes each updated booking's first _calendar reference via find(), so for the multi-reference bookings this diff introduces, other hosts' references are never targeted and their credentials are never fetched (the per-reference DB credential lookup added for the non-recurring path is not applied here). Cancelling a recurring collective booking deletes only events reachable via the organizer's own credentials and only the first calendar reference of each remaining booking, so every other host's future events stay on their calendars while the cancellation API reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, the recurring-cancellation path (inside `if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings)`) still iterates only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar"))` and, for each `updBooking`, selects a single calendar reference via `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. With this diff changing bookings to potentially have multiple `_calendar` references (now handled elsewhere via `.filter(...)` + per-reference credential DB lookup), this recurring branch will delete at most one reference per updated booking and will not fetch/use non-organizer credentials per reference. As a result, other hosts’ calendar events for future instances can remain undeleted while the code continues without surfacing failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is a silent no-op when the organizer has no destinationCalendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null), discarding every member's destination calendar collected in teamDestinationCalendars. For a collective event whose organizer has no destinationCalendar but whose members do, the members' chosen destination calendars are silently dropped and the create falls back to the all-credentials path, placing their events on default calendars (Google 'primary') instead of the calendars they configured, with no error or log indicating the feature did not apply.

adjudication.rationale:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists:
```ts
destinationCalendar: ... ? [...] : ... ? [...] : null,
```
Later, for collective team events, member calendars are appended via optional chaining:
```ts
evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);
```
If the organizer has no destination calendar, this is a silent no-op and all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped. Downstream, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` only takes the destination-calendar-specific path when `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`; otherwise it falls back to the “all credentials” path. In Google Calendar, that fallback can default to `"primary"` (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`), matching the finding’s described misplacement.
